title: Reassembly of upper weights from restrictions to complementary pieces
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\Qlb\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. For a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $S_0$ put $S=S_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the common-stage coefficient category $D^b_c(S,\Qlb)$ and its constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart]. Weil objects and equivariant morphisms are fixed pairs as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Mixed upper bounds and $D_{\le w}(S_0)$ have the meanings of [def-weil-punctual-weights; def-weil-complex-weights].

Let $j_0:V_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ be an open immersion with closed complement $i_0:T_0\hookrightarrow Y_0$ [def-weil-open-immersion; def-weil-closed-immersion], all schemes separated of finite type over $k_0$. Use derived pullbacks [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], compact-support extension $Rj_{0!}$ [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support], and $Ri_{0*}$ [def-weil-derived-direct-image], with their induced Weil structures. Fix $u\in\mathbf R$ and suppose
$$Rj_{0!}(D_{\le u}(V_0))\subseteq D_{\le u}(Y_0),\qquad Ri_{0*}(D_{\le u}(T_0))\subseteq D_{\le u}(Y_0).$$
For every constructible Weil complex $M$ on $Y_0$, if $j_0^*M\in D_{\le u}(V_0)$ and $i_0^*M\in D_{\le u}(T_0)$, then $M\in D_{\le u}(Y_0)$. In particular, for a constructible Weil sheaf $G$ on $Y_0$, if $j_0^*G$ and $i_0^*G$ are $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $u$, then so is $G$. In this last assertion $G$ and its restrictions are placed in degree zero.

proof.text: Put $A=Rj_{0!}j_0^*M$ and $B=Ri_{0*}i_0^*M$. The restriction hypotheses give $j_0^*M\in D_{\le u}(V_0)$ and $i_0^*M\in D_{\le u}(T_0)$. Apply the two assumed preservation inclusions to these particular objects. They give $A,B\in D_{\le u}(Y_0)$, with the same bound $u$ and no cohomological shift.

source.place: Part 2, complex form: the two outer terms have the required upper weight bound.

proof.text: Base change the complementary immersions to $k$. Apply [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] on $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, with $\Lambda=\Qlb$ and underlying complex $\operatorname{For}M$. It supplies the localization triangle with outer terms $\operatorname{For}A$ and $\operatorname{For}B$; its Weil-equivariance clause applies because the immersions and Weil datum come from $k_0$. Thus its arrows are morphisms of the fixed pairs in the statement, while distinguishedness is asserted in $D^b_c(Y,\Qlb)$. Apply the outer-term criterion [lem-zl-open-closed-weight] with $X_0=Y_0$, $K=M$ and $w=u$ to the bounds of step 1. It gives $M\in D_{\le u}(Y_0)$. No triangulated structure on the category of fixed pairs is used.

source.place: Part 2, complex form: target devissage by lem-zl-open-closed-weight.

proof.text: For the sheaf assertion, [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] applies to the base-changed immersions between finite-type $k$-schemes at $\Lambda=\Qlb$. Hence $G,j_0^*G,i_0^*G$ all lie in their constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart]. By the standard truncations of [prop-constructible-truncations], a heart object $F$ has $\mathcal H^0(F)=F$ and $\mathcal H^n(F)=0$ for $n\ne0$. These identifications respect the induced Weil data, since Frobenius is a scheme automorphism and that node makes truncations and cohomology commute with its pullback. The zero sheaf is mixed of weights at most every real number, using the length-zero filtration in [def-weil-punctual-weights]. Thus the definition in [def-weil-complex-weights], degree by degree, says that such an $F$ belongs to $D_{\le u}$ exactly when $F$ is mixed of weights at most $u$: degree zero has bound $u+0$, and all other degrees are zero.

source.place: Part 2, sheaf form: exact pullbacks and the degree-zero interpretation of the upper bound.

proof.text: By step 3 the sheaf hypotheses are precisely $j_0^*G\in D_{\le u}(V_0)$ and $i_0^*G\in D_{\le u}(T_0)$. Apply the complex assertion of steps 1--2 to $M=G$ placed in degree zero. It gives $G\in D_{\le u}(Y_0)$, which step 3 identifies with the required mixed upper weight bound on $G$.

source.place: Part 2, final sentence of the sheaf argument: apply the complex assertion in degree zero.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q44-bb71bab65 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This is a first split of a Q15-created leaf, not a re-split. It has no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. I read Part 2 of lem-zl-morphism-open-closed-reduction.proof.md (main-20261015). Its complex form ends with 'the target devissage [lem-zl-open-closed-weight]', and its sheaf form applies the same argument to G in degree zero. The item takes the two preservation bounds as hypotheses; the parent supplies them from lem-zl-open-shriek-weight-preservation and lem-zl-finite-pushforward. Step 1 instantiates the hypotheses (elementary). Step 2: the triangle node's hypotheses hold (X separated of finite type, Λ=Q̄_ℓ, the descent and Weil clause apply), and lem-zl-open-closed-weight applies with X_0=Y_0, K=M, w=u. The triangle citation is redundant but harmless. Step 3: lem-a1 makes the restrictions heart objects; prop-constructible-truncations gives H^0(F)=F and H^i(F)=0 for i≠0, compatibly with the Weil data; the filtration with m=0 makes the zero sheaf mixed ≤ any bound. So on the heart, D_{≤u} is equivalent to mixed ≤ u. Step 4 (elementary) puts these together. Both tool uses are accepted: lem-a1 and prop-constructible-truncations are generic and already in the statement closure through def-weil-punctual-weights and def-weil-complex-weights. Both batch-5 flags are accepted. def-weil-local-frobenius-trace is a general definition reached through the item's own weight definitions. lem-pod-texact-truncation-comparison is a generic t-structure lemma. Neither is the trace formula, Poincaré duality, or a step of their proofs. I checked the empty-V_0, empty-T_0, empty-Y_0, M=0 and negative-u cases and found no cycle and no duplicate (rg for 'reassembl' and the item id).
